provenance.pins: inferred - the datasheet (p.1) states only 'Polarity: Indicated by cathode band' and numbers no terminal, and the EasyEDA symbol names both pins 1/2 with no C/A labels. Pin 1 = cathode is the DO-214AC convention, not a reading. CONFIRM AGAINST THE BAND BEFORE PLACING: this is the TPS54360B catch diode, and reversed it is a forward short from SW to GND on every switching cycle.

notes: USED ON THE CONTROLLER as the TPS54360B's catch diode. That part is non-synchronous and 'requires an external catch diode between the SW pin and GND' (TPS54360B datasheet p.26) - it was missing from the BOM until the thermal pass. 60 V blocks the 36 V input; average current is Iout x (1-D) = 0.60 A at the 0.7 A rail load against a 3 A rating; it dissipates 0.30 W. A 1.0 A load assumption, which nothing else in this design uses, would give 0.86 A and 0.43 W instead.

NOT evidenced as in use on the V3 module. C2903825 appears in the .epro2 project library but is not placed on any complete board in that archive: the fully specified sheets are the LED matrix PCB (36 WS2812 + 36 100nF + 3 connectors, no converter) and a v1 variant with an LT1085CT-5. The one sheet that does carry a converter has no LCSC parts assigned.
The figures below are sound arithmetic on an ASSUMED part, not a reading of the built design. Treat them as conditional on the module actually using an SS36.

If it is the catch diode: 3.0 A average forward rectified, 60 V (datasheet p.1). At 36 V in / 5 V out the duty is 0.14, so it carries 2.16 x 0.86 = 1.86 A average at full white, 62% of rating. Dissipates roughly 1 W, the hottest part on the module, with no protection of its own.
designVerdict: SELECTED as D2 - the TPS54360B catch diode, and only that. The eFuse output transient Schottkys (D15/D16) are MBRS3100T3G (C12790): this part is 60 V and would sit at 60% of its rating in continuous reverse bias, where its 0.5 mA leakage costs ten times more standby draw.
